items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Well, no. You don't get to know them more than you'd see them... everybody's glad to see Sedric and all them.

ctx.x: Oh, he was fabulous. So you didn't know him.

Well, no. You don't get to know them more than you'd see them. Like, you'd see Sissle. But you don't run up in Sissle's face. Not me.. Other people run up there and introduced theirselves. I know ...(?). . . "Oh, that's Sissle. He's (?) in the business." So you see him. There's Sissle. There's Claude Hopkins. You see Sam Wooding, and you understand he's coming back, and he came back to America, and everybody's glad to see Sedric and all them. But when they came back, nothin' happened. items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: Later on, I had a friend of mine from St. Louis, Cedric, he was telling me about this boat.

ctx.x: It was a real haunting sound there in the evening.

Just before the city got so commercial, it electrified, you know, the electric wires and all that, you know. And the noise of the trucks, you hit real plain. But later on, as the city got more pussing with cars and cabs and the den of the city would kill off some of the cars. It was a dear to dear I remember once I was on the river front with my grandmother's at his lunch, his lunch pail, she was serving, and the news spread was around me and said, there's that bald eagle in town, this terrific river packet, one…
Who was Cedric? Which Cedric is that?
